A. Annual Fire Inspection Report per SB1205
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a resolution acknowledging receipt of a report on the status of state-mandated annual fire inspections in the City of Santa Monica pursuant to California Health and Safety Code Section 13146.4; and
2. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.

B. Award Contract for Inspection and Maintenance of City’s Stormwater Infrastructure
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt finding s of Categorical Exemption s pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) and Section 15308 (Actions for Protection of the Environment), of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Award RFP# SP 2708 to United Storm W ater, Inc . , a California-based company, to provide inspection and maintenance services for the City’s stormwater infrastructure;
3. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Uni ted Storm Water, Inc, in an amount not to exceed $2,626,457 (including a 10% contingency) for five (5) years, with one renewal option of up to two (2) years in the amount of $1,164,203(including 10 % contingency) for a total amount not to exceed $3,790,66 0 over a 7 year period, with the future year funding contingent on council budget approval.

A. Study Session on the City of Santa Monica's Proposed Games Agreement with the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games Organizing Committee
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15272 (Olympic Games) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CE QA) Guidelines;
2. Hold a study session on the Games Agreement and options and alternatives to host beach volleyball for the LA28 Olympics , weighing the potential benefits of direct involvement against the potential long-term financial and legal risks to the City;
3. Receive public comment; and
4. Provide direction to staff on how to proceed.

A. Public Hearing and Adoption of Resolution Approving the California Municipal Finance Authority (“CMFA”) to Issue Revenue Bonds for the Benefit of 1634 20th Street, LP
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Hold a public hearing under the requirements of the Tax and Equity Fiscal Responsibility Act (“TEFRA”) and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended;
2. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
3. Adopt a resolution approving the issuance of California Municipal Finance Authority bonds in an amount not-to-exceed $45,000,000 for t he benefit of 1634 20th Street LP or a related or successor entity for the purpose of financing or refinancing the acquisition, construction, improvement, and equipping of a multifamily rental housing project located at 1634 20th Street, Santa Monica.

B. Request by Mayor Phil Brock, Vice-Mayor Lana Negrete, and Councilmember Oscar de la Torre that the City Council endorse Proposition 36 on the November 2024 statewide ballot. Proposition 36 makes several key changes related to punishments for theft and drug crimes. First, it increases punishment for some of these crimes. Second, it creates a new treatment-focused court process for some drug possession crimes. Third, it requires courts to warn people convicted of selling or providing illegal drugs to others they can be charged with murder if they keep doing so and someone dies. (Attachments include the full text of the ballot measure and an analysis by the Legislative Analyst’s Office-The CA Legislature’s Nonpartisan Fiscal and Policy Advisor) New Item Received. 8/6/2026
